clue.text: Show how not to do things as tree cut by power, chopped, dies back

definitions.text: Show how not to do things

indicators.note: back, placed after the whole string of pieces, says everything built so far is read from right to left
cut by means the tree word is split open with the power symbol pushed into it

parts.note: the elm is a common tree
P is the physics symbol for power
chopped means axed, cut down
dies, as in dies down, means abates

explanation.surface: Someone explains bad practice by describing a tree being felled and dying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' sits after the last piece but turns the whole assembled run, ELPMAXEDABATES, round. 'dies' means dies down; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a bad example is to model conduct others should avoid copying.

clue.text: Morricone's so called uplifting chic encapsulated by his last trio

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the assembled letters are read from the bottom upwards
encapsulated by means the word for chic sits inside the other piece

parts.note: his refers to Morricone, whose surname ends in the three letters O, N, E
chic means fashionable, in

explanation.surface: A remark about the composer Morricone's elegant style shown in his final three works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' stands for Morricone himself, so 'his last trio' is the surname's last three letters. 'uplifting' turns the assembled OINNE upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennio is the first name of the film composer Morricone, so it is what he was called.

clue.text: I go scot-free and I stray when I should take responsibility?

indicators.note: stray means wander off course, so the letters of the preceding words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellious youngster boasts of escaping punishment and wandering off just when maturity is expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of 'I go scot-free and I' rearrange to give the phrase; 'stray' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The age of discretion is the point at which a person is deemed old enough to be accountable for their own choices.

clue.text: For me, life's meaningless, a billion and 15 lives chiefly trivial

parts.note: 15 points to the answer of 15 across, a word meaning not rational; a surd is an irrational number
lives means exists, is

indicators.note: chiefly means only the leading letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A nihilist declares life pointless, a billion lives being mostly trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 15 across (irrational) gives SURD, the mathematical term for an irrational root.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurdist holds that human existence has no inherent meaning, so this is the creed such a person would voice.

clue.text: Previously more noblemanlike?

definitions.meaning: previously means at an ... time, sooner
an earl is a nobleman, so the comparative of an imagined adjective meaning like an earl

explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means before now; whimsically it is also the comparative of earl-like, more like a peer.

clue.text: Auditor's notice will confuse

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the following words are what is heard spoken

parts.note: a notice is an ad, and will contracts to 'll, giving ad'll

explanation.surface: A warning that an accountant's official notice will bewilder people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but means a hearer: 'ad'll' (notice will) spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle someone is to muddle their thinking, synonym for bewilder.

clue.text: Reporting without spelling mistakes?

parts.note: news told in pictures rather than words can contain no misspellings, since there is no text to spell

explanation.definitionFit: Journalism done through photographs reports the news with images, so spelling never comes into it.

clue.text: Former enemy with dog up in shed

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece is placed inside the word for enemy

parts.note: an enemy is a foe

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for dog is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them

explanation.surface: An old adversary, with a dog, is holed up in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the dog word to LIAT in this down entry. 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is the verb, to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To exfoliate is to slough off skin or bark in flakes, which is to cast it away.

clue.text: Nude scene cut or, alternatively, —?

indicators.note: alternatively suggests the letters taken another way, a fresh arrangement
cut means the word scene loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A censor's note offering to trim a nude scene, or else show it in full.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last E of 'scene' and rearrange NUDE + SCEN + OR. The dash stands for the answer: the alternative to cutting the scene is leaving it intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncensored means shown in full with nothing removed, the opposite of a cut scene.

clue.text: Ronaldo's header goes in off German scorer

indicators.note: goes in means the picked letter is put inside the next word
header means the first letter, the top of the following name

explanation.surface: A football report: Ronaldo heads one in off a German defender.
explanation.walkthrough: R (Ronaldo's header) goes into OFF. 'scorer' is a composer, one who writes scores, not a goalscorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was a German composer, best known for Carmina Burana, and composers write scores.

clue.text: Perhaps a husky, low speaker

definitions.meaning: a husky is a dog, and a dog is something that barks or woofs
a loudspeaker unit for reproducing bass sounds

explanation.definitionFit: A dog is a barker, as a husky may be; a bass loudspeaker unit handles low-frequency sound.

clue.text: Summer treat involving risk, losing principal and accepting flop

indicators.note: accepting means the trimmed word takes the word for flop inside it
losing principal means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: something involving risk is dicey
to flop is to loll, lounge limply

explanation.surface: A dangerous summer pleasure, a lounger drops the main thing and takes a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing principal' drops the first letter, leaving ICEY, which then takes the flop word inside. 'Summer' is the season, not one who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen lolly on a stick is a classic hot-weather snack.

clue.text: Who's prominent in holiness after journeying Islamically?

definitions.text: Who's prominent in holiness after journeying Islamically?

indicators.note: the letters that stand out at the front of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A question about who is held in high regard for holiness after making a Muslim pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'holiness after journeying Islamically' spell the answer, and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A haji is a Muslim honoured for having completed the pilgrimage to Mecca.

clue.text: Off their (old ma's) rockers

indicators.note: off, as in off one's rocker, means mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A jibe that some elderly mothers have gone off their rocking chairs, mad.
explanation.walkthrough: THEIR + O + MAS rearranged gives the band's name. 'Off their rockers' is the idiom for mad, but 'rockers' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerosmith is an American hard-rock band, so its members are rock musicians.

clue.text: Section of Altiplano I tarried over, suffering phobias?

indicators.note: over means the extracted slice is turned round and read right to left
a section is a slice of the following words, taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A traveller stuck for a while on part of the Andean plateau feels anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The run LANOITARRI sits inside 'Altiplano I tarried', and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Phobias are fears without reasonable basis, so one gripped by them is unreasoning.

clue.text: Left in knot on Thursday 7is this clue

indicators.note: in means the word for left is placed inside the word for knot

parts.note: a tie is a knot
left means departed, went

explanation.surface: A note about someone who left tangled up on Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts TH after TWENTIE. In the printed paper this clue was 20 down, hence 'this clue'; the stray '7' is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition refers to the clue's own position in the printed numbering, the ordinal for number twenty.

clue.text: Nimble-fingered woman watching execution of company in dull employment

indicators.note: in means the company abbreviation goes inside the word for dull

parts.note: dull means trite, hackneyed
employment means use

explanation.surface: A knitter sits watching a beheading while a company does dull work.
explanation.walkthrough: In the French Revolution such women knitted beside the guillotine, so 'execution' is a beheading, not the carrying out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricoteuses were women who knitted while watching executions during the French Revolution.

clue.text: One with a glue rendered hooves

parts.note: un is a dialect or French word for one

indicators.note: rendered suggests boiling down and reshaping, so the letters are made into a new form

explanation.surface: An animal whose hooves have been boiled down into glue.
explanation.walkthrough: UN plus an anagram of A GLUE gives the plural; 'rendered' is apt since hooves are rendered into glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungulae is the Latin-derived plural for hooves or claws.

clue.text: Sequence Blair uses twice when backing director

indicators.note: backing means the four-letter run is reversed

parts.note: Eric Blair wrote as George Orwell, a pen name in which the four-letter run G, E, O, R appears twice in succession

explanation.surface: A remark on a phrase Tony Blair repeated, in support of a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' suggests Tony Blair but means Eric Blair, George Orwell: GEOR GEOR-well. Reversed, the run gives the film director Nicolas Roeg.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Roeg was a British film director, known for Don't Look Now.

clue.text: Exploiting cases of a woman working in a theatre?

indicators.note: cases means the word for exploiting encloses the female pronoun

parts.note: exploiting means using
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a woman employed at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: showing people to their seats is one theatre job, so the answer is a participle of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers guide audiences to seats, so this is a playhouse job.

clue.text: I'm fat-headed, having picked up a dose of mastoiditis

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the run is lifted and read upwards
a dose is a portion of the medical word, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A patient admits to dimness after catching an ear infection.
explanation.walkthrough: TOIDI sits inside 'mastoiditis'; 'picked up' reverses it. The definition is what a dunce would say of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dolt is a fat-head, so the self-description fits a dunce.

clue.text: Shock which confronts church

parts.note: which as a relative pronoun can be replaced by that

explanation.surface: A scandal that faces the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a scandal but means a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick mop, and a thick head of hair is also called a thatch.

clue.text: What's caught with fishing-line may go here

definitions.text: What's caught with fishing-line may go here

parts.words: What's caught with fishing-line may go here
parts.note: describes the basket an angler drops the catch into

explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which anglers keep the fish they land.

clue.text: Someone like Hillary or Barack finally getting animosity completely abandoned by Left

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the name is used
completely abandoned means every L is taken out, not just one

parts.note: animosity means ill will
L is the standard abbreviation for left, here every one in the word

explanation.surface: A New Zealander or Obama finally feels hostility as the political Left deserts them.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Hillary, the climber, was a New Zealander. K from Barack, then ILLWILL with all four Ls removed leaves IWI.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwi is the informal word for a New Zealander, as Edmund Hillary was.

clue.text: Infidel led off is not sharp

indicators.note: off means wrong or gone bad, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An unbeliever being taken away looks blurry.
explanation.walkthrough: INFIDEL + LED rearranged; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-defined means vague or blurred, lacking clear outlines.

clue.text: Tenth hit managed in modest game

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for modest

parts.note: modest means humble

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenth success achieved in a low-key contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges TENTH HIT to NTTHETHI, which sits inside the modest word. 'modest game' reads as a low-key contest, but only 'game' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a children's party game in which players search for a hidden sewing thimble.
